title: Excerpt from Verified Complaint for Breach of Fiduciary Duty and Fraud
text:
IN THE COURT OF CHANCERY OF THE STATE OF DELAWARE

CAROLINE DUNN, derivatively on behalf of MERIDIAN HOLDINGS, INC., a Delaware corporation,

Plaintiff,

v.

WILLIAM R. HASTINGS, JENNIFER HASTINGS, and GRAYLOCK ADVISORS, LLC,

Defendants.

C.A. No. 2025-0342-KSJM

VERIFIED COMPLAINT (EXCERPT)

Plaintiff Caroline Dunn, by and through her undersigned counsel, brings this derivative action on behalf of Meridian Holdings, Inc. ("Meridian" or the "Company"). The factual allegations are based upon personal knowledge and investigation of counsel, except as to matters specifically pleaded on information and belief.

1. Plaintiff Caroline Dunn, a stockholder of Meridian, brings this action to redress breaches of fiduciary duty by the individual defendants, who constitute a controlling group. Defendant William R. Hastings ("Bill" or "Hastings") served as CEO and Chairman from 2010 until his resignation in January 2025. Defendant Jennifer Hastings ("Jen") is William’s spouse and served as General Counsel. Defendant Graylock Advisors, LLC ("Graylock") is a Delaware limited liability company controlled by William Hastings that received improper payments from Meridian.

2. The Company is a diversified financial services firm headquartered at 1420 Commerce Street, Wilmington, Delaware 19801. Its principal place of business is 1420 Commerce Street, Wilmington, Delaware 19801.

3. Jurisdiction is proper under 10 Del. C. § 341 and the doctrine set forth in In re Cornerstone Therapeutics Inc. Stockholder Litig., 115 A.3d 1173 (Del. Ch. 2015), and In re Dole Food Co. Stockholder Litig., 2015 WL 5052214 (Del. Ch. Aug. 27, 2015).

4. On April 12, 2022, the board approved a transaction whereby Meridian purchased a portfolio of distressed assets from Graylock for $12 million, based on a valuation prepared by Hastings. The purchase price was grossly inflated. As noted in the deposition of former CFO Robert Dunn, "[Hastings] told me the price was non-negotiable and that I should not question it." Exhibit A, Dep. of Robert Dunn, at 45:12-15 (Bates MERID-00012345).

5. Defendant William R. Hastings is a natural person and a resident of Texas. His date of birth is November 14, 1968. His Social Security number is 456-78-9012. He can be reached at (512) 555-0173 and by email at whastings@graylockadvisors.com. His Delaware Bar Number is 4567.

6. Defendant Jennifer Hastings holds Delaware Bar Number 8901. Her email is jhastings@meridianholdings.com. Her telephone number is (302) 555-0198.

7. Graylock Advisors, LLC maintains a policy with National Surety Corp., Policy Number NSU-883-2021-ALF, covering its fiduciary liability. The VIN of the company vehicle assigned to William Hastings is 1HGBH41JXMN109186.

8. The challenged transaction lacked a legitimate business purpose and constituted waste. As the Court held in similar circumstances in In re Tesla Motors, Inc. Stockholder Litig., 124 A.3d 1050 (Del. Ch. 2015): "A fiduciary cannot use corporate assets to enrich a related party without full disclosure and approval by disinterested directors." That principle applies squarely here.

9. Count I – Breach of Fiduciary Duty. Delaware law imposes upon directors and officers the duty of loyalty and care. See 8 Del. C. § 102(b)(7). The complaint alleges that Hastings breached his duty of loyalty by causing Meridian to enter into the unfair transaction with Graylock.

10. Count II – Unjust Enrichment. Defendants were unjustly enriched at the expense of Meridian.

11. Plaintiff demands judgment as follows: (a) rescission of the asset purchase; (b) disgorgement of all profits obtained by defendants; (c) damages in an amount to be proven at trial; (d) pre- and post-judgment interest; and (e) such other relief as the Court deems just.

Respectfully submitted,

BAILEY & SHAW LLP
By: /s/ Michael T. Ryan
Michael T. Ryan (Bar No. 3456)
1000 Market Street, Suite 200
Wilmington, DE 19801
(302) 555-0201
mryan@baileyshaw.com

title: Excerpt from Complaint for Breach of Fiduciary Duty and Misappropriation
text:
IN THE COURT OF CHANCERY OF THE STATE OF DELAWARE

PATRICIA ANDERSON, derivatively on behalf of BRYANT ENERGY CORP., a Delaware corporation,

Plaintiff,

v.

DEBORAH BRYANT, DANIEL BRYANT, and BRYANT CAPITAL MANAGEMENT, LLC,

Defendants.

C.A. No. 2025-0411-LWW

VERIFIED COMPLAINT (EXCERPT)

Plaintiff Patricia Anderson, by and through her counsel, brings this derivative action on behalf of Bryant Energy Corp. ("Bryant Energy" or the "Company").

1. Plaintiff Patricia Anderson ("Pat" or "Anderson") is a stockholder of Bryant Energy and brings this action to remedy breaches of fiduciary duty and self-dealing by the defendants. Defendant Deborah Bryant ("Deb" or "Ms. Bryant") served as CEO and a director of the Company from 2005 until October 2024. Defendant Daniel Bryant ("Dan") is her son and served as CFO. Defendant Bryant Capital Management, LLC ("BCM") is a Delaware LLC controlled by Deborah and Daniel that received undisclosed management fees from the Company.

2. The Company is a renewable energy firm with its principal executive offices at 501 Innovation Drive, Dover, Delaware 19904.

3. This Court has jurisdiction pursuant to 10 Del. C. § 3114 and the principles articulated in In re Cornerstone Therapeutics Inc. Stockholder Litig., 115 A.3d 1173 (Del. Ch. 2015), and In re Ezcorp Inc. Consulting Agreement Derivative Litig., 2016 WL 301245 (Del. Ch. Jan. 25, 2016).

4. In 2023, the Company paid $3.5 million in consulting fees to BCM without board approval. As stated in the board minutes, "[Deborah Bryant] directed the payment to be made without a formal vote." Ex. C, Board Minutes, Jan. 15, 2023, at 3 (Bates BRY-00009876).

5. Defendant Deborah Bryant resides in Texas. Her date of birth is March 22, 1970. Her Social Security number is 123-45-6789. Her business phone is (469) 555-0301. Her email is dbryant@bryantenergy.com. She holds Delaware Bar Number 5678.

6. Defendant Daniel Bryant resides in Texas. His email is daniel.bryant@bryantcap.com. His telephone is (214) 555-0402. His SSN is 987-65-4321. His date of birth is July 9, 1978.

7. Bryant Capital Management, LLC holds a liability insurance policy with Federal Insurance Company, Policy Number FID-342-2022-RT. The company vehicle assigned to Deborah Bryant is a 2023 Tesla Model S, VIN 5YJSA1E27PF123456.

8. The fees paid to BCM were excessive and lacked any reasonable justification. As the court noted in In re Trados Inc. Shareholder Litig., 73 A.3d 17 (Del. Ch. 2013): "Fiduciaries must demonstrate the entire fairness of transactions with a controlling stockholder."

9. Count I – Breach of Fiduciary Duty. 8 Del. C. § 102(b)(7) does not exculpate defendants for acts of bad faith. The complaint alleges that Ms. Bryant and Daniel acted in bad faith by enriching BCM at the Company's expense.

10. Count II – Unjust Enrichment. Defendants were unjustly enriched.

11. WHEREFORE, Plaintiff demands judgment: (a) requiring disgorgement; (b) awarding damages; (c) ordering restitution; (d) awarding costs and fees; and (e) granting such other relief as is proper.

Respectfully submitted,

ANDERSON & CRANE LLP

title: Excerpt from Complaint for Breach of Fiduciary Duty and Self-Dealing
text:
IN THE COURT OF CHANCERY OF THE STATE OF DELAWARE

SUSAN HARRIS, derivatively on behalf of GRAYSON TECHNOLOGIES, INC., a Delaware corporation,

Plaintiff,

v.

THOMAS GRAYSON, MARTIN GRAYSON, and GRAYSON FAMILY TRUST,

Defendants.

C.A. No. 2025-0503-SG

VERIFIED COMPLAINT (EXCERPT)

Plaintiff Susan Harris, by and through her counsel, brings this derivative action on behalf of Grayson Technologies, Inc. ("Grayson Tech" or the "Company").

1. Plaintiff Susan Harris ("Sue" or "Harris") is a stockholder. Defendant Thomas Grayson ("Tom" or "Mr. Grayson") served as President and Chairman from 2015 until his termination in December 2024. Defendant Martin Grayson ("Marty") is his brother and served as Vice President of Operations. Defendant Grayson Family Trust ("Trust") is an irrevocable trust established by Thomas and Martin that holds a controlling interest in the Company.

2. The Company is a software development firm located at 78 Innovation Way, Newark, Delaware 19711.

3. Jurisdiction exists under 10 Del. C. § 341. See also In re Cornerstone Therapeutics Inc. Stockholder Litig., 115 A.3d 1173 (Del. Ch. 2015); In re Nine Systems Corp. S'holders Litig., 2014 WL 4383127 (Del. Ch. Sept. 4, 2014).

4. In 2023, the Company loaned $2 million to the Trust at an interest rate of 1%, far below market. The loan was never disclosed to the independent board members. As the whistleblower Edward Kim stated: "[Thomas Grayson] told me to process the wire without a promissory note." Ex. F, Interview Tr., at 12:8-10 (Bates GRAY-00023456).

5. Defendant Thomas Grayson resides in Texas. His date of birth is May 5, 1965. His SSN is 234-56-7890. His business phone is (972) 555-0601. His email is tgrayson@graysontech.com. His Delaware Bar Number is 6789.

6. Defendant Martin Grayson resides in Texas. His SSN is 345-67-8901. His date of birth is August 12, 1970. His phone is (972) 555-0702. His email is mgrayson@graysontech.com.

7. The Grayson Family Trust maintains an account at First Delaware Bank, Account Number 9876543210. The Trust holds a fidelity bond with Surety Bond Corp., Policy Number SB-445-2023-XY. The VIN of the Company's vehicle used by Thomas is WBA3A5C50DF123456.

8. The loan to the Trust constituted waste and a breach of the duty of loyalty. As the Court stated in In re Oracle Corp. Derivative Litig., 132 A.3d 1 (Del. Ch. 2016): "A fiduciary may not use corporate assets for personal benefit without full disclosure and disinterested approval."

9. Count I – Breach of Fiduciary Duty. 8 Del. C. § 102(b)(7) does not shield defendants from liability for intentional misconduct. The complaint alleges that both Thomas and Martin acted with scienter.

10. Count II – Unjust Enrichment. Defendants were unjustly enriched by the below-market loan.

11. Plaintiff requests: (a) rescission of the loan; (b) disgorgement; (c) compensatory damages; (d) costs and fees; (e) such other relief.

Respectfully submitted,

title: Excerpt from Complaint for Breach of Fiduciary Duty and Usurpation
text:
IN THE COURT OF CHANCERY OF THE STATE OF DELAWARE

MARK LEWIS, derivatively on behalf of TANNER BIOPHARMA, INC., a Delaware corporation,

Plaintiff,

v.

STEVEN TANNER, PATRICIA TANNER, and TANNER RESEARCH INSTITUTE, INC.,

Defendants.

C.A. No. 2025-0612-PAF

VERIFIED COMPLAINT (EXCERPT)

Plaintiff Mark Lewis, by and through his counsel, brings this derivative action on behalf of Tanner BioPharma, Inc. ("Tanner Bio" or the "Company").

1. Plaintiff Mark Lewis ("Mark" or "Lewis") is a stockholder. Defendant Steven Tanner ("Steve" or "Mr. Tanner") served as CEO and Chairman until February 2025. Defendant Patricia Tanner ("Pat" or "Ms. Tanner") is his spouse and served as Chief Scientific Officer. Defendant Tanner Research Institute, Inc. ("TRI") is a Delaware nonstock corporation that usurped corporate opportunities belonging to the Company.

2. The Company is a biopharmaceutical company with principal offices at 200 Discovery Drive, Wilmington, Delaware 19808.

3. Jurisdiction is proper under 10 Del. C. § 3114. See In re Cornerstone Therapeutics Inc. Stockholder Litig., 115 A.3d 1173 (Del. Ch. 2015); In re Walt Disney Co. Derivative Litig., 907 A.2d 693 (Del. Ch. 2005).

4. In 2024, Steven Tanner caused the Company to assign a promising drug patent to TRI for $1, without board approval. As former R&D director Dr. Helen Wu testified: "[Steven Tanner] said the patent was worthless, but I knew it was worth millions." Ex. G, Dep. of Dr. Helen Wu, at 78:4-8 (Bates TANN-00034567).

5. Defendant Steven Tanner resides in Texas. His date of birth is January 15, 1962. His SSN is 456-78-1234. His phone is (281) 555-0901. His email is stanner@tannerbiopharma.com. His Delaware Bar Number is 7890.

6. Defendant Patricia Tanner resides in Texas. Her SSN is 567-89-2345. Her date of birth is June 20, 1964. Her phone is (281) 555-1002. Her email is ptanner@tannerbiopharma.com.

7. TRI holds an account at Wilmington Trust, Account Number 8765432109. The Institute has a liability policy with Chubb, Policy Number CHU-556-2024-QW. The VIN of the Company's vehicle used by Steven is 1C4RJFAG6FC123456.

8. The assignment of the patent was a breach of the duty of loyalty. As noted in In re CBS Corp. Stockholder Derivative Litig., 2021 WL 2685955 (Del. Ch. June 30, 2021): "A fiduciary cannot divert a corporate opportunity without first offering it to the corporation."

9. Count I – Breach of Fiduciary Duty. 8 Del. C. § 102(b)(7) does not apply to bad faith. The complaint alleges that Mr. Tanner and Ms. Tanner acted in bad faith and for personal gain.

10. Count II – Usurpation of Corporate Opportunity. The patent was developed using Company resources and belonged to the Company.

11. Plaintiff prays for: (a) imposition of a constructive trust; (b) disgorgement; (c) damages; (d) fees; (e) other relief.

Respectfully submitted,

title: Excerpt from Complaint for Breach of Fiduciary Duty and Waste
text:
IN THE COURT OF CHANCERY OF THE STATE OF DELAWARE

NANCY PARKER, derivatively on behalf of RIVERSIDE MANUFACTURING, INC., a Delaware corporation,

Plaintiff,

v.

JONATHAN RIVERS, VICTORIA RIVERS, and RIVERSIDE REALTY TRUST,

Defendants.

C.A. No. 2025-0718-VCG

VERIFIED COMPLAINT (EXCERPT)

Plaintiff Nancy Parker, by and through her undersigned counsel, brings this derivative action on behalf of Riverside Manufacturing, Inc. ("Riverside" or the "Company").

1. Plaintiff Nancy Parker ("Nan" or "Parker") is a stockholder. Defendant Jonathan Rivers ("Jon" or "Mr. Rivers") served as CEO and Chairman from 2008 until his resignation in March 2025. Defendant Victoria Rivers ("Vicki" or "Ms. Rivers") is his daughter and served as General Counsel. Defendant Riverside Realty Trust ("RRT") is a Delaware statutory trust that owns the Company's factory building and charged excessive rent.

2. The Company is a manufacturing firm with its principal place of business at 100 Industrial Boulevard, Georgetown, Delaware 19947.

3. Jurisdiction is proper under 10 Del. C. § 341. See In re Cornerstone Therapeutics Inc. Stockholder Litig., 115 A.3d 1173 (Del. Ch. 2015); In re RJR Nabisco Inc. S'holder Litig., 1989 WL 7036 (Del. Ch. Jan. 31, 1989).

4. From 2020 to 2024, the Company paid RRT rent of $1.2 million per year, triple the market rate. As former CFO William Harris noted: "[Jonathan Rivers] insisted we sign the lease without negotiation." Ex. H, Dep. of William Harris, at 32:5-7 (Bates RIV-00045678).

5. Defendant Jonathan Rivers resides in Texas. His date of birth is October 10, 1960. His SSN is 678-90-1234. His phone is (713) 555-1201. His email is jrivers@riversidemfg.com. His Delaware Bar Number is 8901.

6. Defendant Victoria Rivers resides in Texas. Her SSN is 789-01-2345. Her date of birth is February 14, 1985. Her phone is (713) 555-1302. Her email is vrivers@riversidemfg.com.

7. Riverside Realty Trust has an account at PNC Bank, Account Number 7654321098. The Trust holds an insurance policy with Travelers, Policy Number TRV-667-2025-AB. The VIN of the Company's vehicle assigned to Jonathan is 2C3CDXBG3KH123456.

8. The excessive rent constituted waste. As the Court held in In re Citigroup Inc. S'holder Derivative Litig., 964 A.2d 106 (Del. Ch. 2009): "Waste occurs when consideration is so inadequate that no person of ordinary business judgment would approve."

9. Count I – Breach of Fiduciary Duty. 8 Del. C. § 102(b)(7) does not protect against waste. The complaint alleges that Mr. Rivers and Ms. Rivers wasted corporate assets.

10. Count II – Unjust Enrichment. RRT was unjustly enriched.

11. Plaintiff demands: (a) reformation of the lease; (b) disgorgement of excess rent; (c) damages; (d) fees; (e) other relief.

Respectfully submitted,

PARKER & WALKER LLP
